executor_result.summary: Bind source_evidence clocks to revision provenance with explicit source record ID and revision per clock, while maintaining backward compatibility and adding focused test coverage.

instructions: In part2/capital_flow/handoff.py, fix the compact source_evidence revision/provenance ambiguity introduced by independent freshness clocks. Today latest_effective_at_ms may come from one PIT-visible row while latest_available_at_ms/latest_observed_at_ms come from a different later-arriving revision, but the entry exposes only the newest-effective row's provenance/attribution fields, so consumers cannot identify which source record/revision established each freshness clock. Preserve the existing independent timestamp/age semantics exactly. Add explicit compact provenance for each of the three selected clocks (effective, availability, observed), identifying at minimum source_record_id and revision for the row that supplies that clock; deterministic tie-breaking must be stable and must not select a non-visible row. Keep the existing provenance/attribution fields tied to the newest-effective economic row for backward compatibility. Preserve PIT filtering, context/scoring role separation, explicit missingness, context visibility, raw/audit separation, and frozen scoring. Add one focused regression in test_v1_handoff.py extending the existing two-row revision case: row A supplies latest effective, row B supplies latest available/observed; assert the clock provenance points effective to row A and availability/observed to row B. Also cover missing available_at deterministically if the implementation exposes an availability provenance value: it must be explicit null/None when no visible row has availability. Do not change scoring, provider collection, or unrelated handoff fields.
title: Bind source_evidence clocks to revision provenance
